subject: EU in-region processing — evidence & technical follow-ups
messages:
From: Martin Schulz <martin.schulz@medicorp.de>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Meier <legal@medicorp.de>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: EU-only processing & SCCs — initial evidence request

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this. MedicoRP is running a pilot that will include PHI-derived metadata from our EU clinics. Before we move forward we need confirmation and evidence on a few items:

- Can you commit to EU-only processing for customer data at rest and in-flight (including model KV caches and logs)? If not, what parts of the flow leave the EU?
- Are the EU processing controls enforced by region routing + dedicated tenant isolation, or do you rely on contractual SCCs/fallbacks?
- For SCCs / Schrems II: do you provide a completed SCCs addendum and a technical appendix showing data flows?
- Data retention & deletion: how do you evidence deletion across all layers (storage, backups, logs, caches)? Time-to-delete SLA candidates we are considering: 24h or 7d.
- KMS: can we bring our own keys (BYOK) for keys that encrypt customer payloads in-region?

Can you share any templates / evidence (diagram, checklist, sample attestation) we can give to our security & legal teams? We're targeting an internal deadline of May 16 to decide.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to jump on a call if needed.

Best,
Martin
Senior IT Security Manager
MedicoRP

Hi Martin — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (infra/arch) for technical detail and Neha (privacy/compliance) for retention/SCCs artifacts. Below is a concise summary; we'll attach a checklist + diagram in a follow-up.

Short answers up front:
- EU-only processing: Yes — we can route and process customer payloads entirely within EU regions for hosted deployments, including KV cache and transient token caches.
- SCCs vs routing: We offer in-region processing as the operational control. SCCs are provided as a contractual layer (we can attach the SCCs addendum + technical appendix).
- Deletion evidence: We can provide per-tenant deletion logs, storage object tombstone records, and an export of the deletion audit for the retention window.
- BYOK/KMS: Supported for Private (VPC) deployments and select Dedicated configurations; we'll list constraints.

Karthik / Neha — action items: 1) share the architecture diagram (EU routing + guarantees), 2) exportable deletion evidence formats and timelines, 3) copy of SCCs appendix and recommended redlines for MedicoRP legal. Martin — we'll aim to get the checklist and diagram over by EOD PST Monday so you can circulate to your team.

Best,
Grace O'Connor

Subject: Re: EU-only processing & SCCs — initial evidence request

Hi Martin / Grace,

Following up with the technical specifics and attachments (pushed to the drive link and attached a small PNG for quick reference). Key details:

1) Routing & in-region guarantees
- For Hosted EU deployments we run inferencing on physical compute located in EU cloud regions (AWS eu-west-1 / GCP europe-west3, depending on customer preference).
- The control plane can remain in a separate region, but we do not route customer payloads (requests, KV cache, model inputs/outputs) through non-EU compute when "EU-only processing" is selected at the tenant level.
- Persistent storage, model shards (for cached custom models), and ephemeral KV caches are provisioned on EU storage classes. Replication across regions is disabled by default.

2) SCCs and contractual layering
- We provide the standard SCCs addendum + a technical appendix that maps fields to flows. The appendix describes which logs may contain metadata and the retention safeguards (pseudonymisation where applicable).

3) BYOK/KMS
- BYOK is available for Private deployments (customer-managed KMS in VPC); for Hosted we offer customer-managed keys in supported cloud KMSs where possible, but there are limitations around key escrow for multi-tenant hosting. We will enumerate allowed configurations in the checklist.

4) Deletion & evidence
- Deletion workflow: 1) tenant object delete request -> mark objects for deletion + async GC; 2) remove from primary storage and clear KV caches; 3) emit a deletion audit event per object with timestamp + operator id; 4) background job purges tombstones and cleans backups per retention policy.
- Evidence we can provide: deletion audit CSV (object id, timestamp, stage), storage tombstone export, and a short certifying statement signed by our compliance team for the requested deletion window.
- SLA: operationally we can commit to a 72-hour deletion window for hosted EU tenants as standard; 24-hour deletion SLA can be offered for Dedicated/Private with negotiated runbooks and evidence-sharing (this typically requires reserved capacity or explicit orchestration for faster GC).

Attachments included: inregion-arch-diagram.png (high-level), MedicoRP_SCCs_Checklist.xlsx (checklist + configuration matrix).

If you want, we can run a short 30-min tech deep-dive and demo of the deletion evidence export (I can correlate sample audit lines to objects).

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
